newsitem.title: UK: BBC and BSkyB at odds over digital TV - paper.
newsitem.headline: BBC and BSkyB at odds over digital TV - paper.

text.p: Talks between the BBC and pay television operator BSkyB about digital satellite transmission of BBC programes are close to breaking down, the Daily Telegraph reported on Monday.
The two have been unable to agree on how much the BBC should pay for transmission, BSkyB seeking 300 million stg more than the BBC is offering, the report said.
The BBC is planning to develop additional programming, both free and pay channels, to exploit the extra capacity offered by digital.
BSkyB plans to launch 200-channel digital satellite services into the UK early next year while cable and terrestrial digital services are also set for launch within the next year or so.
The BBC has said it wants to make its programmes available by all three distribution mechanisms.
